components.description: The single hot action for joining or creating a room.

components.css: .ds-roster { border: 1px solid #3a3349; border-radius: 16px; padding: 20px; background: rgb(18 16 27 / 55%); color: var(--ink, #f6f0e6); box-shadow: 0 20px 60px rgba(0,0,0,0.18); font-family: 'Bricolage Grotesque Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-roster-head { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px; margin-bottom: 20px; } .ds-roster-head h2 { margin: 0; font-size: 24px; line-height: 1.2; letter-spacing: -0.03em; } .ds-roster-count { color: var(--cyan, #7df9e7); font-weight: 800; } .ds-roster-row { min-height: 64px; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 16px; border-top: 1px solid var(--line, #2b2639); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line, #2b2639); padding: 12px 0; } .ds-roster-index { width: 36px; height: 36px; flex: 0 0 auto; display: grid; place-items: center; border-radius: 9999px; background: #221c30; color: var(--violet, #b9a4ff); font-size: 14px; font-weight: 800; } .ds-roster-row div { min-width: 0; flex: 1; } .ds-roster-row strong { display: block; } .ds-roster-row em { margin-left: 8px; color: var(--cyan, #7df9e7); font-size: 12px; font-style: normal; } .ds-roster-row small { display: block; margin-top: 3px; color: #8d869b; } .ds-roster-row i { width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--cyan, #7df9e7); box-shadow: 0 0 12px rgba(125,249,231,0.65); } .ds-roster-note { margin: 20px 0 0; color: #8d869b; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.5; } .ds-sr-only { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0,0,0,0); white-space: nowrap; }

narrative.overview:
The interface should feel like admission to a live after-dark hunt: immediate, coded, and operational rather than promotional. Ink-black violet space, oversized bone-white instructions, precise monospace signals, and a single hot orange action establish the event atmosphere without turning the screen into Halloween decoration.

The world is intentionally sparse. Fine lavender rules and translucent field-sheet surfaces organize live state while cyan marks the connection signal. The shipped login, lobby, and host views keep essential tasks prominent on narrow phones and allow the same hierarchy to breathe on desktop.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black, edge-to-edge canvas with subtle violet and cyan ambient light.
Heavy, tightly tracked Bricolage Grotesque headlines paired with coded monospace metadata.
Safety-orange primary actions, cyan connection signals, and lavender emphasis.
Thin rules, modest 12–16px corners, and large room codes instead of generic dashboard chrome.
Text accompanies every color-coded state; touch controls remain at least 44px tall.

rules.name: The Signal Color Rule
rules.body: Cyan means connected, current, focused, or successfully completed; never use it as a competing primary action.

rules.name: The One Hot Action Rule
rules.body: Orange identifies the immediate action. Keep it rare enough that the next step is obvious at a glance.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Bricolage speaks to people; monospace identifies rooms, channels, and terse system state.

rules.name: The Short-Display Rule
rules.body: Reserve the largest, tightest type for brief commands or rallying lines. Longer explanation stays in body scale.

rules.name: The Camera-Ready Density Rule
rules.body: Keep authentication and lobby UI compact, touch-safe, and portrait-first; desktop adds breathing room, not a second marketing story.

rules.name: The Local Glow Rule
rules.body: Glows belong to the brand mark, an active orange keyline, or a live cyan presence dot—not to whole panels or decorative text.

rules.name: The Selective Radius Rule
rules.body: Curve containment and touch controls; keep information rules, room-code utilities, and structural lists crisp.

dos: Do keep Safety Orange focused on the primary action and its supporting signal mark.
Do use Signal Cyan with explicit connection, focus, current-player, or success copy.
Do keep controls at least 44px tall and preserve the 3px cyan focus-visible outline.
Do use monospace selectively for room codes, channel labels, and terse state.
Do preserve the single-column phone hierarchy before introducing the shipped large-screen split.
Do honor reduced-motion preferences; the shipped room-signal entrance collapses to effectively immediate motion.
donts: Don't place authentication inside a white card or turn the desktop split into a marketing panel.
Don't use cyan as a second primary action color or rely on color alone to communicate connection state.
Don't round every surface; squared rules, lists, and room-code utilities are part of the field-pass character.
Don't spread glows across large panels, paragraphs, or display headlines.
Don't substitute decorative Halloween typography for the shipped Bricolage-and-monospace pairing.
Don't introduce hover-only meaning on these touch-first surfaces.
